newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF says may give Ukraine new stand-by, delay EFF.
newsitem.headline: IMF says may give Ukraine new stand-by, delay EFF.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) may issue a small stand-by loan to Ukraine until it meets conditions for a larger, long-term loan meant for countries ready for structural reforms, a senior IMF official said on Friday.

Patrick Lenain, IMF representative in Ukraine, told Reuters the stand-by loan would be considered instead of a three-year, $2.5-3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) if parliament failed to complete the Fund's wish list before it closed in mid-July.

"That would give them the time to bring together the measures. The EFF could come later on," Lenain said, adding the long-term programme was intended for countries ready to implement large-scale structural reforms.
Ukrainian officials had first expected to receive the EFF late last year but the process was held up by the passage of the budget, approved only on Friday.

But Lenain said the stand-by was proposed, when an IMF mission visited the former Soviet republic last week, if parliament did not fulfil all its conditions this session. Ukraine said recently it had passed 27 of 41 IMF conditions.

Lenain said the IMF had also wanted Ukraine to cut payroll taxes from 52 percent to 40 percent as a first step, in an attempt to legalise the undeclared economy -- estimated by Western analysts to account for up 60 percent of all economic activity.
"We were expecting significant cuts in payroll taxes," he said.

The budget was to be passed in concert with a series of nine tax reform laws but only two -- on value-added tax and taxation of business profits -- have been approved with the balance to be considered by the end of the year.
